sources.entry: oauthlib - A generic and thorough implementation of the OAuth request-signing logic.

summary.one_liner: OAuthLib is a Python framework implementing OAuth 1 and OAuth 2 request-signing and provider/client logic without tying to a specific HTTP library or web framework.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes OAuthLib as a generic, spec-compliant implementation of OAuth1 (RFC 5849) and OAuth2 (RFC 6749) logic for Python 3.8+. It does not assume a particular HTTP request object or web framework, so it can be grafted onto HTTP client libraries or used to add OAuth provider support to web frameworks. The README lists existing packages built on it: django-oauth-toolkit, django-allauth, flask-oauthlib, Flask-Dance, pyramid-oauthlib and bottle-oauthlib. It also points to requests-oauthlib for OAuth support in the requests library. The README states the core of both OAuth1 and OAuth2 is complete for providers as well as clients. Full documentation is hosted on Read the Docs, which the README calls still sparse.
use_cases: add OAuth client support to an HTTP library
build an OAuth provider in a web framework
add OAuth login to Django, Flask, Pyramid or Bottle apps
notable: Framework-agnostic: does not assume a specific HTTP request library or web framework
Supports both provider and client sides, per the README
Existing integrations for Django, Flask, Pyramid and Bottle are listed in the README
caveats: Documentation is described as quite sparse
Low-level library: web framework and HTTP glue must be written or supplied by a package
keywords: log in with oauth in python
